references.text: Moses receives the two tablets of the testimony from God on Mount Sinai, written with the finger of God.
God commands Moses to carve out two new stone tablets after the first ones were broken, and to write the same words on them.
Moses comes down from Mount Sinai for a second time, holding the two tablets of the testimony in his hand.
Moses recounts how the Lord gave him the two stone tablets, written with God's finger, containing all the words the Lord spoke on the mountain.
Moses describes how he carved out new tablets and placed them in the ark, according to the Lord's command.
Describes that there was nothing else in the ark except the two stone tablets which Moses laid down in it at Horeb.
Paulus refers to the stone tablets and contrasts them with the law of the Spirit written on the tablets of the heart.
Refers to the ark of the covenant which contained the stone tablets with the words of the law.
Contrast between descending with the first (broken) tablets and ascending with the restored ones.
Connection between the Lord's promise to give the tablets and their actual delivery.
Direct retelling of the same event with additional details about God's presence.
